recipes.name: White Chocolate Macadamia Nut Cookies IV

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

In a medium bowl, cream together the butter and sugar. Stir in the egg and vanilla. Combine the flour, baking soda and salt, stir into the creamed mixture. Finally, stir in the white chocolate and nuts. Drop cookies by heaping teaspoonfuls onto an ungreased cookie sheet, about 2 inches apart.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven, until lightly browned. Cool on wire racks. When cool, store in an airtight container.

raw_recipe.headline: White Chocolate Macadamia Nut Cookies IV
raw_recipe.description: These have become the family's new favorite cookie! The white chocolate gives a rich taste to these cookies. I guarantee you will love them.

review.reviewBody:
These cookies were great! I didn't change a thing, and they were just perfect. I got about 36 average-sized cookies out of this recipe, and each one was delectable. I have tried other recipes which include brown sugar, and have determined that brown sugar has too bold a flavor for the delicate white chocolate and macadamia nuts. Trust me-- this recipe is absolutely fabulous.

UPDATE: My husband and I love these cookies so much that we make the dough, freeze the uncooked dough balls on a cookie sheet, put them in a zip-lock bag, and keep a supply handy at all times. Whenever we crave them, we'll pop a few out of the bag and bake at 350 for about 15-18 minutes. Awesome.

Finally a recipe that doesn’t call for softened butter & brown sugar! Both of which I discovered made them flat & gooey. I doubled this recipe without doubling the nuts/chips. I didn’t add the salt as my Macademia nuts consisted with sea salt. I refrigerated the dough for 30 min prior to baking. I compared my pampered chef stone with a stick free pan and found that my stone made them spread nicely. They turned out good on my other pan but cooked darker and crispier. Love this recipe, now just have to package nicely for my boyfriend.

I added 1 cup of coconut as well as doubling the basic cookie recipe, but keeping the nuts & chips amount as listed here. I made extra-large cookies using a 1/4 cup scoop, baking them at 350 degrees for 12 - 13 minutes. I also found that rolling the dough balls in sugar and refrigerating them for at least 30 minutes before baking made slightly-crisp cookies on the outside, and soft, chewy cookies on the inside. In a taste test of two, we both greatly preferred those cookies rolled in sugar and refrigerated to the standard preparation.

These are great cookies. The only change I made is to only use about 2-3 oz of nuts; 6 oz is a lot. And in my oven, they only need to cook for 7-8 minutes. They come out soft in the middle and a little crunchy on the outside. And I get about 20 cookies, not 24. 

And useful hint, I put them in the fridge for a few minutes after scooping them onto the baking tray. This keeps them from spreading when they cook. Also, I use an ice cream scooper for more uniform-sized cookies.
They turned out great! I doubled the recipe and used a 12oz bag of Nestle'swhite chocolate morsels. Plenty of white chocolate. I used a small 1 inch scoop and it made 99 cookies instead of 48.

I followed recommendation and double recipe but used about 9 0z nuts and one bag white chocolate chips. Also, each batch I tried different timing- definitely that soft chewy cookie if you only bake for 9 minute let rest in tray briefly and then to cooking rack. Even when cooked just over 10 minutes they are still very soft and delicious!
Great recipe! 2 changes...I added ~4 oz more chopped white chocolate and chilled the dough ~15 mins before forming balls to ensure they kept their shape. Came out perfectly. Thank you for posting.

I just finished these cookies and they are phenomenal! I did do a few things different only bc I wanted to play with texture and flavors. I followed the recipe but I did add a 1/4 cup of buttermilk bc it works with the baking soda to give rise and it also made a tender cookie with a light crispness on the outside. I added a pinch of cinnamon, and 3/4 tsp vanilla and 1/4 tsp of almond extract. these were the best white chocolate macadamia nuts cookies ever. Thank you

Made the recipe exactly as follows. Definite keys to success:
- butter must be ever so slightly softened, does not need to be left out overnight for example
- chopping the macadamia nuts and white chocolate into small pieces is key because the amount of nuts and chocolate to batter is overwhelming - the smaller the nuts and chocolate are, the easier it is to incorporate into the small amount of batter
- oven temperature must be 375 - so use your oven thermometer if needed (my oven runs 25 degrees on the hot side!)
- if your kitchen feels too warm, refrigerate the dough

I used white chocolate chips - that yes, I chopped up. Again, glad I did because it makes sure that every bite of your cookie has chocolate and nuts. As everything is small, you don't get gaping holes in the cookies, or uneven baking.
Used 1/4 c. Sugar and subbed the rest with stevia, also added an extra 1/2 tsp vanilla. 34 delicious tablespoon sized cookies!

I accidentally added 1 tbsp of vanilla extract instead of the 1 tsp and I didn't have any nuts so I added 1/4 cup of coconut flakes and I knew they weren't going to turn out right so I put them in a muffin pan instead and oh my gosh they were amazing white chocolate, coconut muffins! My family loved them. I always have a hard time making cookies lol. Next time I'll pay more attention to the tsp vs the tbsp.

I followed this recipe (almost) exactly -I added a tsp more vanilla than called for. I was quite concerned that the dough to chocolate/nut ratio was way off. There was SO much white chocolate & nuts, it seemed to be only those with bits of dough throughout. I thought it would be dry or over-powered by white chocolate However, after baking, they came out perfectly. I cooked for a two - three minutes longer to get that golden crunch on the bottom and they are absolute perfection. Surprisingly not too sweet, soft in the middle w/a crisp edge. 5-stars.
Excellent cookies, I followed the recipe as stated. Family loved them. As another review mentioned, I baked a dozen and froze the rest of the dough to bake as needed. Will make these again.
Nice recipe. Made it with pecans, 5 oz and 5 oz chocolate. That s already plenty. Will do with less sugar next time. Bit too sweet
This recipe was simple and easy and the cookies came out great!!!
Delicious!!
Added about 2-3 oz of English toffee just adds to the already wonderful cookie

I followed this recipe almost exactly as written, with the exception that I added a little more white chocolate chips which is usually my habit for recipes that call for chips. My whole family thought it was rather bland, and nobody ate another cookie from the batch after the initial cookie they ate to taste. Maybe we like things a little sweeter than this, but I won't be making it again.

These are sweet and good. I made as written but used a little over 4 oz of nuts and about 6 oz of white chocolate and that was more than enough. I also subbed country crock plant butter for the butter and it worked great.
Great cookies - easy to add stuff to - will be my new easy cookie recipe go-to
